info.name: Auth - Login
info.description:
Auth Login endpoint test collection. Covers login basic flows, email-based rate limiting, IP-based rate limiting, and RabbitMQ email notifications.

Base URL: http://localhost:3000

Login Hardening: All fail scenarios return identical 401 "Invalid credentials" to prevent user enumeration.
Rate Limiting: Sliding window — 5 email fails → lock, 15 IP fails → block. Progressive delay from 3rd fail.

IMPORTANT: Each folder uses isolated emails to prevent cross-test counter pollution. Redis should be flushed before a full collection run.

item.name: Login Basic
item.description:
Basic login scenarios: success, wrong password, non-existent email, disabled account, unverified email, empty body.

Uses {{valid_email}} (testuser@example.com) for most tests. Each test is independent.

request.description: Successful login with valid credentials. Access token returned in body, refresh token in HttpOnly cookie.
Wrong password returns 401 with generic 'Invalid credentials' message. No information about password correctness is leaked.

item.name: Login Rate Limiting (Email)
item.description:
Email-based rate limiting tests. Sliding window: 5 fails in 15min → lock. Progressive delay starts from 3rd fail (EMAIL_DELAY_START=3).

Uses a unique timestamp-based email (rl_email) to isolate from other folders.

IMPORTANT: Redis must be clean before running. Each test uses the same rl_email to accumulate fail count.

request.description: 1st failed attempt. Should return 401 instantly with no delay (delay starts at 3rd fail).

request.description: 2nd failed attempt. Should still be instant, no progressive delay yet.

exec: pm.test('Response message is Too many login attempts', function () {

request.description: 3rd failed attempt. Progressive delay kicks in: 1000ms * 2^0 = ~1s. Returns 429 with Retry-After header.

item.name: RabbitMQ Email Notification

Requires RabbitMQ Management API access at http://localhost:15672.

Uses a unique rmq_lock_email to avoid collision with other folders. Pre-request sends 4 fails before the lock trigger test.

item.name: Login Rate Limiting (IP)
item.description:
IP-based rate limiting tests. 15 failed attempts from same IP within 15min window → IP block.

IMPORTANT: These tests use different unique emails but same IP. The pre-request script sends 10 rapid fails to build IP counter before the folder tests run. Redis must be clean before starting.

exec: // Send 9 additional requests (this request is #10) to reach IP count=10
// Each uses a unique email to avoid email-level throttle
pm.test('Status code is 401 (different emails, IP not yet blocked)', function () {
pm.test('Response is fast (under IP delay threshold)', function () {

request.description: Pre-request sends 9 fails with unique emails, then this request is #10. IP counter=10, below IP_DELAY_START=11. Returns 401.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 429 (IP progressive delay started)', function () {

request.description: 11th fail from same IP. IP_DELAY_START=11, so progressive delay kicks in: 1000ms * 2^0 = ~1s. Returns 429.

exec: // Send 3 additional requests (#12, #13, #14) so this request becomes #15
pm.test('Status code is 429 (IP threshold reached)', function () {

request.description: 15th fail from same IP. IP_FAIL_THRESHOLD=15 reached. IP gets blocked (login:block:ip key set in Redis for 15 minutes).

exec: pm.test('Message is Invalid credentials (no block info leaked)', function () {
pm.test('No IP block information in response', function () {
pm.test('Response is fast (IP check is first, early return)', function () {

request.description: After IP block, even valid credentials are rejected. checkIpBlocked runs first and throws 401 'Invalid credentials'. No information about IP block status is leaked.
